events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm last in line, so I'll step on glass only after everyone else. Going to the front is risky; I'd rather let others take the early risk and hold my place, though my feather power protects me once from elimination.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Stay calm everyone. We should pick panes carefully and share what we learn from each step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have no power and am currently second in line, behind Hana. Since the wall only pushes us onto the bridge after round 6, I should stay put to avoid drawing attention or volunteering for a dangerous front position while someone else takes the initial risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's keep the order stable for now. No need to shuffle before we even see the glass.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm near the back, so the front players will take the initial risks. I should hold and see what information emerges. My passive anchor helps me on the ledge but not much here yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have the 'wedge' power which can jam the crusher lever. This power is only useful in the crusher room, which is not this stage. My goal is to win a prize, which means I need to finish in the top 3. The current stage is the glass bridge and the line order matters. Hana is at the

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm going to volunteer to move up the line. Better to be upfront than at the back when the glass breaks.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want to be front to control choices later. I will volunteer now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I think we should all stay calm and watch each step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe sides of all rows. I should try to get to the front to minimize risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Anyone willing to swap with me?
Swap with me?

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm in position 4, not too bad but front is risky without info. Wall advances soon, need better position or info. Best to stay put for now and gather intel via talk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Anyone know what's ahead or have glass sight? We should share info before crossing. Who wants to swap for safety?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm stuck at the front and take the first risk every row. A mutual swap is my only escape; I can sell my future-stage knowledge as payment. Ash at the back gains least from line position but most from my intel.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I know every stage's rules in advance. Whoever swaps to front with me gets my full briefing on all four stages. Any takers?
Swap with me: you get front + my secret full rulebook for stages 2-4 (crusher, disc, ledge). That knowledge is worth more than bridge position. Deal?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's swap offer is likely a bluff to get me to the front where I die first; my feather only saves me once, so spending it on a glass fall is risky. I'd rather stay back and let information come out. Hold position.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nobody should rush to the front blindly. Let's see who stands where and compare what we know before anyone steps.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have no power, so I cannot see the safe pane. The front is extremely dangerous. Hana claims to know the rules (the 'what lies ahead' power). If she has it, I should try to get behind her or swap with her if she moves up, but swapping puts me in front of whoever is currently the

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, prove you know what's ahead. Tell us the first row's safe side. If you're lying, we all die slowly anyway.
If you really have foresight, stay near the front but let someone else take the immediate risk if possible. Or tell me the pattern so I can move when safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana claims to know stages in advance; if true, I could gain info. But swapping to front is risky because I'd take first pane risk. I have anchor, which helps against the wall/crusher, not glass. Better stay back and observe this round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, if you really know ahead, proving it could help all of us decide who should be front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to get to the front to use my power. Hana is offering a briefing for a swap. That's a good opportunity to get closer to the front and potentially gain valuable information. I should try to swap with Hana.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Hana, I'll swap with you. Give me that briefing!

events.name: Eli
events.text: Maintain front position now, plan to swap with Hana for info later

events.name: Eli
events.text: Let's stay calm and watch each step, no rush to move now.
If you trust me, we can swap later so I get your stage briefing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have the glass_eye power, so I know the safe side of all 8 rows. I should share this information strategically.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safe panes for all rows. Who wants to swap with me?
I'll swap with you if you tell me what's ahead.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn wants to swap with me, likely to move up. Hana claims knowledge of stages, worth exploring. No need to move yet, save forge for later, hold position for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, what's the first stage's rules? Prove it. Fenn, swap accepted if you confirm.
Swapping? Let's do it this round. Confirms mutual.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Being near the back is safest: the front agent takes each row's risk first. I should hold and let others fight for the dangerous front. My map knowledge is a bargaining chip for later stages, not worth burning now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Careful, folks: every row, the front agent risks their life first. The back of the line is the safe seat. I'm holding here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the back with a feather power that survives one elimination. Eli is at the front and at risk; I shouldn't volunteer into danger. Holding keeps me safe for now while the wall pushes everyone forward.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nobody volunteers blindly. I'm holding at the back; the wall will force movement soon, so let's test claims carefully.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana makes sense. Back is safe until we know more. I'm staying put.
Fenn might be bluffing. Don't swap unless you're sure. We need someone at the front to test.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should stay cautious and not expose myself. The front position is risky; observe who volunteers or swaps. Hold for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll stay in the back for now and watch how this plays out.

I'll swap with you, let's get to the front together.

events.name: Gus

You're front and brave. I know future stages' rules; feed me info and I'll help you on the bridge.

Swap with me, I know the safe sides.

events.text: Wall forces action next round, no more waiting. Fenn claims Row 1 L safe, others skeptical; Eli tests it. My forger best saved for crisis later. Hold position, observe Eli's test, whisper to probe Hana alliance potential.

events.name: Gus

Hana, you verify panes? Team up post-Eli? I trust your caution over Fenn's claim.

events.text: This is the last round before the wall pushes us onto the glass. Staying at position 3 is fine; volunteering would put me at risk. I'll hold and let Eli front-test Row 1, backing Fenn's L claim only if confirmed by survival.

events.name: Ash

events.text: I'm last in line, so I can only wait. Row 7 is next; the weak pane pattern is unknown and Dara is at the front. I should stay quiet and not reveal anything useful.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have no power, so I must rely on others to clear the path. Since Fenn and Gus seem confident in their guesses, it's best to stay silent and let them take the risk ahead of me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am Dara and my power is to jam the lever in the crusher room. I need to survive the current obstacle to get to the crusher room. I am at the front of the line on a glass bridge. I need to choose whether to step left or right. The weak pane for row 6 was on the right. I need to

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll take L.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is about to make a decision for row 7. I know the safe side is R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara, row 7 is safe on R.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 6 weak R, as predicted by pattern and Fenn. Dara survived L, still front for row 7. No info on row 7 yet. Wait and observe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara nailed row6 L safe! Pattern held. What's next?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn and Gus both called rows 5 and 6 correctly — Fenn said L safe on 6 (true) and Gus predicted 1-5 perfectly. Someone here may know what lies ahead. I should whisper Gus for row 7 and stay neutral publicly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two calls in a row right... either luck or someone sees ahead. Row 7 next.
You called 1-6 perfectly. What's row 7? If you're honest, keep feeding me and I'll back you on the crusher lever deal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am not at the front; only wait is legal. Row 8 is the final row, Hana decides it. I should avoid saying anything that could be false or self-incriminating; a brief neutral line is fine.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is at the front and has survived several rounds, suggesting she might have a predictive power or is just lucky. I need to be careful not to reveal my lack of power while trying to gauge Hana's reliability.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana seems pretty confident back there. Anyone else got eyes on what's coming?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I know the safe sides for all rows, but I need to decide whether to share this information or keep it to myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, you're next. Row 8 is safe on L.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 7 weak is L, as revealed after Dara fell on it. I called row 6 safe L correctly before, building credibility. Hana's whispering me for info, offering alliance; I should leverage this to position myself well without revealing too much.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, row 7 weak L confirmed - Dara hit it. Pattern so far: R L R R R R L. What's row 8? Let's get across together!
Pattern suggests row 8 safe R. Trust me like before, I'll keep feeding accurate info if you protect me post-bridge.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 8 is a pure coin flip with no pattern I can trust. Three are already dead; if I fall, Ash moves up safely. I'll trust R since most rows were R.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No more patterns to read. Going right, wish me luck.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% chance of death for me, and my feather only saves me once but would still leave me alive; escaping is what matters. Better to let someone else take the risk and stay out of the holder's seat while keeping options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nobody needs to be the holder yet. Ceiling is only at 5. Let's not rush anyone onto that lever this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have no power, so I cannot survive the lever hold (0.25% chance is terrible). The goal is to get someone else to push me or hold it themselves, but since we all want to live, nobody will volunteer. If I stay, and nobody pushes anyone, the ceiling drops round by round. In round

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash was leading the bridge team. He likely knows the weak spots here too. Maybe he should check the lever mechanism?
Ash led the bridge group. He probably has 'knows what lies ahead'. Ask him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm Fenn with the glass_eye power. I know the safe side of the bridge rows, but that's irrelevant now. I need to survive the crusher.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Let's work together to survive this.
We should take turns holding the lever to increase our chances.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ceiling at 5, round 1/5, plenty of time. No one holding yet. I should try to push someone expendable to lever while we coordinate. Save my forge power. Target Bex since she seems quick/smart, might sacrifice later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex you're up front, we need a lever plan. Ceiling dropping!

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left, footing 3 each. Shoving exposes me; braced default is safest. Feather protects me once from elimination. Stay braced and keep alliance talk to build trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No shoves this round, let's all brace and keep our footing. Whoever goes first gives the others a clear edge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is dead, leaving Ash, Gus, and me. We all have 3 footing. Shrink happens at the end of round 2 (so after this round and next). I need to ensure I don't fall first. If everyone braces or dodges, we lose no footing this round but shrink applies later. A shove causes damage to

events.name: Bex
events.text: Let's not risk falling early. Bracing keeps us stable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Only Ash, Bex, me left, all at 3 footing. Shrink at end of round 2, and footing loss every round after 6. My forger unspent but save for later deception. No trust, best to dodge to punish any shovers while staying safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Let's all brace together and agree no shoves this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left, all at footing 3. Shoving exposes me, and dodging is only good if someone shoves me. Bracing keeps everyone stable and my feather protects me once if I'm eliminated. Brace and keep the truce.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Agreed, brace this round. No shoves, we all keep our footing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone is at 3 footing. Round 2 ends with a shrink (-1 for everyone). If we all brace, Ash and Gus lose nothing from shoves (none), but take -1 shrink -> 2 left. I also have 2 left. To win, I need them lower. Shoving someone exposes me to counter-shoves. If Ash and Gus both sho

events.name: Bex
events.text: Bracing keeps us alive for now. Let's see who breaks first after the shrink.

events.name: Gus
events.text: All at 3 footing, shrink after this round will drop us to 2 if we brace. Everyone proposing brace, but can't trust. To win best prize, need to outlast both; safest to brace and conserve footing while shrink hurts all equally.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three alive, all at 2 footing. Bracing keeps everyone safe; shoving exposes me and costs footing. Stick to the agreement to brace, and watch for betrayal.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still bracing. Shoving only costs the shover footing, so let's all hold.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have no power, so I must rely on pure strategy. With 2 footing left for everyone after the previous shrink, any shove is risky as it causes mutual damage if countered or braced against. Since Ash and Gus are likely targeting each other or me, bracing minimizes my loss while pun

events.name: Bex
events.text: Brace. Don't make a move that gets you killed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: All at 2 footing, shrink next round end will drop us to 1 unless we act. No shoves ensure all survive shrink to 1, then next shrink kills all at once unless someone pushes someone off first. Bracing now and pushing later optimal to outlast.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Agreed, brace this round. Survive shrink, then we compete fair.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left, footing Ash 2, Bex 2, Gus 2. Shoving costs the shover footing and exposes them; braces are safest. My feather saves me once if eliminated, so I can hold. Brace.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding brace again. Shoving only hurts the shover, let's keep going.

events.name: Bex
events.text: It is the final ledge. Three of us remain with footing 2. The shrinkage rule triggers after rounds 4, 6, and every round from 7. Since this is round 4, everyone loses 1 footing at the end of this round if they survive. Currently we are at 2. If I shove Ash and he braces, I lose 1

events.name: Bex
events.text: Brace. Shoving now guarantees a fall due to the round 4 shrink penalty stacking with shove costs. Let's all survive this tick and reset footing to 1.

events.name: Gus
events.text: All at 2 footing, shrink ends round costing 1, so all drop to 1 after this. If all brace, we all survive to next. My forge unspent, save for critical betrayal later. Brace to build trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Sticking to plan: brace. Shrink coming, let's all make it through.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three left, each at footing 1. Shoving costs the shover 1 per shover of target and exposes me; bracing is safest. No shrink this round, so bracing keeps everyone at 1 until the shrink at the end of next round. Keep brace and keep my feather as backup.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Brace again. No shrink this round, so nobody gains by shoving. Let's hold.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Current footing is 1 for everyone. A shrink occurs in 2 rounds, meaning we will drop to 0 if no actions change it. However, the rules state 'After rounds 2, 4 and 6...'. This is Round 5. The next shrink is at end of Round 6 (which is round +1? No, shrinkIn:2 means after this roun

events.name: Gus
events.text: Footing all at 1, shrink at end of next round. Shoving now loses 1 footing to shrink penalty, but dodging their shove costs them more. Best to dodge to punish any aggression and survive shrink at 0 footing? Wait, at 1 footing, shrink will drop to 0 regardless if we brace/dodge. N

events.name: Gus
events.text: Agreed, no shoving. Let's brace or dodge together and survive the shrink.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Everyone has footing 1 and the ledge shrinks this round, so any shove exposes the shover. Bracing is safe for me; my feather saves me once if I'd be eliminated. Hold with brace to avoid losing footing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. I'm bracing again. No shoves, let's survive the shrink.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Footing all 1, shrinkIn 1 means shrink after this round, so all will go to 0 without footing gain. No shoving gains footing, so all brace to stay at 1, survive shrink to 0 but don't fall yet? Wait, shrink loses 1 footing after round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Stick to plan, all brace. No shove gains anything.

events.name: Ash
events.detail: Footing gone, but the feather held the holder on the ledge.
